# arrow

[arrow.apache.org](https://arrow.apache.org) · OSS-Fuzz: [projects/arrow](https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/bd2ce21991a94a362b92fb1bf25f86d5a1a60842/projects/arrow)

**Status: available.** 4 of OSS-Fuzz's 6 fuzz targets have statements. 16 binaries, 441 MB. 28 statements: 0 proved, 0 known false, 0 suspected false, 14 blocked by the model, 14 open.

Built from arrow (commit `70f5c269`).

## At a glance
| harness | what it does | checks beyond "does not crash" | statements |
|---|---|---|---|
| [arrow-csv-fuzz](arrow-csv-fuzz/) | Five readers (serial table, threaded table, streaming, CountRowsAsync with and without newlines_in_values) run on the same bytes; their tables / row counts are NOT compared with each other. | none | 7, 7 blocked by the model |
| [arrow-ipc-file-fuzz](arrow-ipc-file-fuzz/) | Checks 2 properties (listed below); the first, a differential check: Differential IPC reading: the file reader without and with PreBufferMetadata, and (when the file read succeeded, schemas match incl. metadata, batch counts and endianness agree) the stream reader over the same bytes, must produce identical batches (RecordBatch::Equals with nans_equal) and identical custom metadata; a mismatch aborts. | none | 7 |
| [arrow-ipc-stream-fuzz](arrow-ipc-stream-fuzz/) | ToString() on each batch that validated (printing must not crash). | none | 7 |
| [parquet-arrow-fuzz](parquet-arrow-fuzz/) | Metadata, statistics, bloom filters (100 random FindHash probes) and page indexes decoded; results discarded; the three batch-size reads are not compared with each other. | none | 7, 7 blocked by the model |

Not included: **arrow-ipc-tensor-stream-fuzz** (not built yet); **parquet-encoding-fuzz** (not built yet).

## What the statements say, for arrow
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch arrow
    ./oft verify-sha arrow

By hand: download `arrow-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.10.0](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.10.0), unpack it into `projects/arrow/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; an OSS-Fuzz testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [apache/arrow](https://github.com/apache/arrow) at `70f5c269ae8d154f57f7a7ec6babe6e0685ed6ec`, built with its own build scripts
- Harnesses: unmodified
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. A binary whose SHA-256 differs after a rebuild with it is a bug: please open an issue.
